requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation of `requirements.references.util` has implementing code reachable from an {impl} item, and a test that runs it.

**1. Provide the built-in `habeas:util` with the quoted text.**
- `src/builtins.rs#const[BUILTINS]` defines `habeas:util` and permits only `ReferenceKind::Cite`.
- `src/builtins.rs#impl[Builtin]/fn[text]` extracts the quoted block from `md/requirements/references.md` after the `:::{req} util` marker. The requirement text is therefore the single source for the built-in's text.
- The test `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` asserts the start and end of that text. It also asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md`. It checks that unknown names such as `habeas:none` and `habeas:other` do not resolve.

**2. Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary.**
- `Builtin::check` rejects any other role with "built-in habeas:util may only be referenced with {cite}".
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]` calls `check` for every built-in reference and records the error. Its {impl} is marked for `requirements.references.util`.
- The unit test asserts `check` accepts `Cite` and rejects `Impl` and `Test`.
- `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` exercises these cases end to end:
  - an inline citation, a fenced citation with commentary, and a bare fenced citation, all accepted;
  - an `{impl}` and a `{test}` citation, rejected with the expected error at the expected line.

**3. An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review.**
- `src/citations.rs#fn[citation_items]` drops items with no citation other than `habeas:util`, using `items.retain`.
- The integration test asserts no "missing citation review" error for the `inline`, `fenced`, and `bare` items. It asserts the review is still required for `mixed`, which also cites `rules.ready`.

**4. A citation of `habeas:util` MUST cover its item under `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.**
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[covering_reference]` returns `builtin.check(kind).is_ok()` for built-ins.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[unreferenced_items]` applies that to comments and to closed comment fences.
- The integration test asserts there is no "function X has no recent coverage" error for the inline, fenced, and bare cases. It asserts `implemented` and `tested` stay uncovered.

All four obligations are implemented by the {impl}-marked items, or by code those items call. No unspecified behavior turned up. The error for unknown `habeas:*` names is covered by `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which `validate_references` also marks.

text: :::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. The reviewer MUST assess, for each citation,
whether the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition
changes, and whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
